findings.title: Negative denial cache causes stale denies with no invalidation
findings.body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go Check() first returns Allowed=false on permDenialCache hit and only sets that entry when a full DB check denies (line 154). The entry lives for shortCacheTTL (30s) and is never invalidated when permissions change. Consequence: if a user is denied once then granted access (e.g. creator of a new dashboard/folder, role/team change), subsequent Checks for that exact name/parent are short-circuited to deny for the TTL window, re-introducing the exact bug the PR claims to fix and extending denial beyond the existing permCache staleness.

findings.title: List still serves stale permission cache with no DB fallback
findings.body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go List() uses getCachedIdentityPermissions and, on hit, lists directly from the cached scope map without verifying freshness. Check() was changed to fall back to the DB when the cached map does not contain the requested resource, but List() has no equivalent revalidation. Consequence: newly created dashboards/folders will still be missing from list responses for up to shortCacheTTL even when Check() would now allow them, leaving the user-visible fix incomplete.

findings.title: Denial and permission caches share overlapping keyspace on shared backend
findings.body: In pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go userPermCacheKey() and userPermDenialCacheKey() both use the prefix namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action, with the denial key just appending "_" + name + "_" + parent. All cacheWrap instances share the same underlying cache.Cache. Consequence: with underscores in UIDs/actions/names (all joined by _ with no escaping or distinct prefix), a permission key can equal a denial key for different parameters, so a Set on one type overwrites the other and a Get unmarshals bool JSON as map[string]bool or vice versa, causing lost entries, cache misses, and either stale allows requiring DB reload or lost denials.
